newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PDL confident of meeting yr profit target.
newsitem.headline: PDL confident of meeting yr profit target.

text.p: Electricial equipment and plastics manufacturer PDL Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday it was confident of achieving its forecast of full-year net profit of NZ$12.4 million.
PDL earlier reported a 6.5 percent fall in half-year net profit to $7.04 million for the six months to September 30.
Total revenue for the half year rose 10.3 percent to NZ$170.5 million thanks to exports rising 34.3 percent and sales by overseas subsidiaries, up 46 percent.
"Notwithstanding a weakening in revenue and margins with our Plastics and Asian companies, we are anticipating a much stronger second half for our group compared with last year," the company said.
"The stronger performance is coming through from PDL Industries Australia Pty and our New Zealand manufacturing subsidiaries PDL Industries and PDL Electronics."
It said the six-month result was in line with the $12.4 million net profit forecast issued at the annual meeting in September.

Directors declared a reduced interim dividend of 20 cents, down from 27 cents last year, but said this was for cashflow purposes only. They said they anticipated the full year dividend would at least match last year's 40 cents.

Interest costs increased by 88.3 percent to $4.29 million due to higher interest rates and increased borrowings as a result of acquisitions in Australia/Asia (OJ Nilsen assets) and in New Zealand (minority stakes in Modempak and MasterTrade).

The result included an unusual gain of $1.64 million relating to the discount received on the purchase of minority interests in MasterTrade Group, as the offer price was less than the net asset backing per share.
